content:
Hi everyone,
we are planning to simplify the proof-pattern syntax in Iris Lean.
At the moment, iintro / icases patterns accept both styles:

  • ⌜h⌝ and %h for pure patterns;

  • □pat and #pat for persistent patterns.
    Our current direction is to standardize on the ASCII forms and only support those going forward:

  • %h for pure patterns;

  • #pat for persistent patterns.
    To be clear, this would only affect proof patterns in iintro / icases. We are not proposing any change to BI notation at the proposition level, so expressions such as ⌜φ⌝ and □ P would remain unchanged.

For example, today we may write:

example [BI PROP] (P Q : PROP) : □ P ⊢ □ Q -∗ Q := by
  iintro □HP
  iintro □HQ
  ispatial HP
  ispatial HQ
  iexact HQ

and 

example [BI PROP] (Q : PROP) : ⊢ <affine> ⌜⊢ Q⌝ -∗ Q := by
  iintro HQ
  icases HQ with ⌜HQ⌝
  istop
  exact HQ

Under the proposed change, these would become:

example [BI PROP] (P Q : PROP) : □ P ⊢ □ Q -∗ Q := by
  iintro #HP
  iintro #HQ
  ispatial HP
  ispatial HQ
  iexact HQ

and 

example [BI PROP] (Q : PROP) : ⊢ <affine> ⌜⊢ Q⌝ -∗ Q := by
  iintro HQ
  icases HQ with %HQ
  istop
  exact HQ

The main motivation is to keep only one notation for each pattern form, which makes the proof-pattern language more uniform and lighter to read.

We would also appreciate feedback on one related question: should we continue to support the ASCII spatial alias *pat, or is ∗ pat sufficient in practice?

My personal opinion is that ⌜h⌝ is quite unwieldy to type, especially compared to %h, since ⌜h⌝ requires typing a unicode character at the end and at the beginning. So I would support getting rid of ⌜h⌝.

In general, I am a fan of having one canonical way to write something instead of multiple equivalent ways. Having one way avoids confusion for newcomers and in general avoids style conflicts. So I think it is good to consolidate the syntax.

For □pat vs #pat I don't have a strong opinion. #pat is the same as in Rocq.

For ASCII *pat vs unicode ∗pat, my opinion is even less strong. I don't think the ASCII * is used anywhere in Iris Rocq, so using it in Iris Lean might be confusing. But one can also make the argument for preferring ASCII over unicode.
Thinking about this again, I find using the ASCII * weird (probably because it is never used by Iris Rocq) and thus to be consistent, it would make sense to use both unicode ∗ and □.

My 2c (which are mostly in agreement with Michael):

In general I think unicode ∗ should never ever be replaced with ASCII * since Lean already uses * for lots of other things. We might even consider adding in an explicit error message in our syntax for when someone uses * instead of ∗. I remember one very frustrating day when I was first learning Iris-Rocq because I accidentally typed * and could not figure what it was telling me. I think I'm fine with removing the ∗ altogether and having spatial patterns default to the separating context, but if it stays it should be unicode.

For □ vs # I don't care. Using ASCII is not really a plus in my book (any file will be filled with unicode anyways) but consistency is probably better than having two options.

And % is a lot less to type than ⌜ ⌝so I agree it should be better to use that.

I agree on using these symbols consistently, and I also prefer typing less. Therefore, I'm in favour of ASCII # and % and making the pattern default to separating context to avoid the * v.s. ∗ confusion.
On a related note about being consistent, I’ve opened a PR to remove commas as separators from the spec pattern: https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/pull/196

Thanks for the suggestions! My current plan is to remove the ⌜h⌝ and □pat syntax and use %h and#pat, to stay consistent with Rocq.

I am still inclined to keep ∗pat, though. In icases, we do need a way to move an intuitionistic proposition into the spatial context, so I do not think we can drop that pattern entirely. Instead, I plan to add a better error message when someone writes ASCII *, along the lines of: “did you mean ∗ (typed as \\ast)?”

Also, while implementing this, I noticed a TODO Michael left about attaching syntax information to cases patterns so that failures in complex icases patterns can be reported more precisely. I will try to address that as well.

Zongyuan Liu said:

On a related note about being consistent, I’ve opened a PR to remove commas as separators from the spec pattern: https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/pull/196

This PR looks good to me. Could you please merge it into master when you have a chance, and maybe also update tactics.md to keep it consistent?

I also have some work in progress on specialization patterns to support >[H] in the presence of AddModal.

Zongyuan Liu said:

making the pattern default to separating context to avoid the * v.s. ∗ confusion.

The default pattern already is to move to the spatial context (in most cases). The ∗ is only necessary in cases where one needs to force something to move to the spatial context. This pattern is called -# in Rocq and we should have an equivalent of it in Iris Lean. (it is important in corner cases, see https://gitlab.mpi-sws.org/iris/iris/-/merge_requests/370)

So it seems the preference is using # for # in Rocq and ∗ for -# in Rocq? There is a slight inconsistency where one is unicode and the other is not, but if this is the preference of the majority, it is fine with me.

Zongyuan Liu said:

On a related note about being consistent, I’ve opened a PR to remove commas as separators from the spec pattern: https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/pull/196

Thanks for this PR, great that you figured this out! I updated tactics.md and merged it.

Yunsong Yang said:

We would also appreciate feedback on one related question: should we continue to support the ASCII spatial alias *pat, or is ∗ pat sufficient in practice?

so it's not possible to do what we did in rocq and just use a plain pat without prefix for the spatial context?
the idea is that this opts-out of the implicit "move to intuitionistic context", hence the notation

@Yunsong Yang implemented the notation change in https://github.com/leanprover-community/iris-lean/pull/194
In summary, □pat becomes #pat and ⌜h⌝ and *pat are gone. If there are no objections, I will merge this.
This change is merged :tada:
